note: Ten things wrong: filler objective, wrong target role, duty bullets, no results, five jobs in four years, two undated roles, typos, gap since June 2023, soft-skill skills list, references line.

model_output.score_comment_short: The resume lists practical duties, but gives little detail about how you performed them.
model_output.score_comment_long: Store opening, customer sales, and training give a useful starting point. Most bullets stop at the task, and two roles have no dates. Add detail to the sales and training bullets and complete the timeline.
model_output.score_plain: A reader can see the jobs you've held, but has limited information for comparing your work with a particular role. The Marketing Manager objective also needs a clearer connection to the experience listed.
model_output.first_impression: Your recent dated role is Shift Lead, with responsibility for opening and closing a store. The Marketing Manager objective points in a different direction from the experience described.
model_output.biggest_gap_example: “Trained new employes when needed” leaves out what you taught, so a reader cannot tell what the training involved.
model_output.summary: Your work spans store operations, wireless sales, warehousing, delivery, and food service. Opening and closing the store is worth keeping because it shows a specific responsibility in your Shift Lead role. The titles and duties point most directly toward shift lead and sales associate work, while the objective names a Marketing Manager position. The resume does not explain how your experience connects to marketing, which makes that target difficult to assess.
strengths: At Buckeye Wireless, you sold phones and accessories and answered plan questions, giving the sales work a recognizable customer context.
The QuickStop role includes training new employees, which distinguishes it from a list of routine store duties.
Forklift use is named in the warehouse role, giving a reader a concrete picture of the work.
gaps: The warehouse and delivery roles have no dates, so their place in your work history is unclear.
The objective names Marketing Manager, but the experience section does not describe marketing work or relevant projects.
The skills list names Microsoft Office without identifying which applications you used or what you used them for.
